title: OSHA construction fall protection practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction fall protection (29 CFR 1926 Subpart M) practice questions, each answer explained and linked to the rule text.

questions.question: Which activity is outside the scope of Subpart M?

options.A: An inspection of workplace conditions before construction work actually starts
options.B: Constructing a leading edge on a deck 8 feet above the ground
options.C: Roofing work on a low-slope roof with edges 12 feet above the ground
options.D: Working on the face of reinforcing steel 10 feet up

questions.explanation: The subpart's provisions "do not apply when employees are making an inspection, investigation, or assessment of workplace conditions prior to the actual start of construction work or after all construction work has been completed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.500, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A gap in a wall is 30 inches high. Under the Subpart M definitions, what is the least width at which it counts as an "opening"?

options.A: 6 inches
options.B: 12 inches
options.C: 18 inches
options.D: 15 inches

questions.explanation: An opening is "a gap or void 30 inches (76 cm) or more high and 18 inches (48 cm) or more wide, in a wall or partition, through which employees can fall to a lower level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.500, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Before employees are put to work on a walking/working surface, what does Subpart M require the employer to determine about it?

options.A: Whether it has been painted a safety color
options.B: Whether it has the strength and structural integrity to support employees safely
options.C: Whether OSHA has inspected it within the past year
options.D: Whether it is level to within 1 inch

questions.explanation: "The employer shall determine if the walking/working surfaces on which its employees are to work have the strength and structural integrity to support employees safely." Employees may work on them only when they have that strength and integrity.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee works 4 feet above dangerous equipment. How must the employee be protected from falling into or onto it?

options.A: By a warning line system alone
options.B: By a safety monitoring system alone
options.C: No protection is required below 6 feet
options.D: By guardrail systems or equipment guards

questions.explanation: Each employee "less than 6 feet (1.8 m) above dangerous equipment shall be protected from falling into or onto the dangerous equipment by guardrail systems or by equipment guards."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In a hoist area, the guardrail is removed and an employee must lean out over the edge of the access opening to guide materials. What protection does the rule require for that employee?

options.A: A personal fall arrest system
options.B: A warning line system
options.C: A safety monitoring system
options.D: A cover over the opening

questions.explanation: When guardrails are removed and an employee must lean through or out over the access opening, "that employee shall be protected from fall hazards by a personal fall arrest system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must protect employees from tripping in or stepping into holes, including skylights?

options.A: Warning lines
options.B: Safety monitors
options.C: Covers
options.D: Positioning device systems

questions.explanation: Each employee on a walking/working surface "shall be protected from tripping in or stepping into or through holes (including skylights) by covers."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an employee on the face of formwork or reinforcing steel who could fall 6 feet or more to a lower level, which of these systems is listed as an allowed choice?

options.A: A warning line system
options.B: A positioning device system
options.C: A controlled access zone
options.D: A safety monitoring system

questions.explanation: An employee on the face of formwork or reinforcing steel must be protected "by personal fall arrest systems, safety net systems, or positioning device systems."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For roofing work on a low-slope roof with an unprotected side or edge 6 feet or more above a lower level, which pairing is one of the combinations the rule lists?

options.A: A controlled access zone and a warning sign
options.B: A safety monitoring system and a fall protection plan
options.C: A warning line system and a positioning device system
options.D: A warning line system and a safety monitoring system

questions.explanation: The listed choices include "a combination of warning line system and guardrail system, warning line system and safety net system, or warning line system and personal fall arrest system, or warning line system and safety monitoring system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On a steep roof with edges 6 feet or more above lower levels, guardrail systems used for protection must have what?

options.A: Toeboards
options.B: A safety monitor
options.C: A warning line 6 feet back
options.D: A control line

questions.explanation: Employees on steep roofs must be protected "by guardrail systems with toeboards, safety net systems, or personal fall arrest systems."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: During overhand bricklaying, an employee reaching more than how far below the level of their walking/working surface must be protected by a guardrail, safety net or personal fall arrest system?

options.A: 24 inches
options.B: 36 inches
options.C: 10 inches
options.D: 6 feet

questions.explanation: Each employee "reaching more than 10 inches (25 cm) below the level of the walking/working surface on which they are working" must be protected by one of those three systems.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A crew is choosing material for the top rail and midrail of a guardrail system. Which material does the rule bar from that use?

options.A: Wire rope at least one-quarter inch thick, flagged at not more than 6-foot intervals
options.B: Steel banding or plastic banding
options.C: Manila rope that is inspected as often as needed to keep its strength
options.D: Wood members that meet the strength requirements

questions.explanation: "Steel banding and plastic banding shall not be used as top rails or midrails." Wire rope is allowed if "flagged at not more than 6-foot (1.8 m) intervals with high-visibility material."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A guardrail system surrounds a ladderway hole that employees use as a point of access. How must the guardrail be arranged at that access point?

options.A: Left open, with a warning sign beside the hole
options.B: Closed off with caution tape only
options.C: Fitted with a toeboard across the access gap
options.D: Provided with a gate, or offset so a person cannot walk directly into the hole

questions.explanation: Guardrail systems around holes used as points of access "shall be provided with a gate, or be so offset that a person cannot walk directly into the hole."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What test load does the jobsite drop-test of a safety net installation use?

options.A: A 400-pound bag of sand about 30 inches in diameter
options.B: A 200-pound steel weight
options.C: An employee wearing a full body harness
options.D: A 100-pound bag of sand dropped from 6 feet

questions.explanation: "The drop-test shall consist of a 400 pound (180 kg) bag of sand 30 ±2 inches (76 ±5 cm) in diameter dropped into the net from the highest walking/working surface" at which employees are exposed to fall hazards.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Tools and scrap pieces have fallen into a safety net during the shift. When must they be removed from the net?

options.A: At the end of the work week
options.B: Only when the net is relocated
options.C: As soon as possible, and at least before the next work shift
options.D: Only when their weight approaches the net's rating

questions.explanation: "Materials, scrap pieces, equipment, and tools which have fallen into the safety net shall be removed as soon as possible from the net and at least before the next work shift."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Outside of elevator shaft construction, two employees use vertical lifelines as part of their personal fall arrest systems. How must they be attached?

options.A: Both to one lifeline, as long as it has a 5,000-pound breaking strength
options.B: Each to a separate lifeline
options.C: Both to one lifeline, if a safety monitor is watching
options.D: One to the lifeline and the other to a guardrail

questions.explanation: "When vertical lifelines are used, each employee shall be attached to a separate lifeline." The only exception is for two employees on a guarded false car during elevator shaft construction.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these does Subpart M say a personal fall arrest system shall not be attached to?

options.A: An anchorage able to support at least 5,000 pounds per employee attached
options.B: An anchorage designed under a qualified person's supervision with a safety factor of at least two
options.C: A self-retracting lifeline that meets the subpart's strength requirements
options.D: A guardrail system

questions.explanation: "Personal fall arrest systems shall not be attached to guardrail systems, nor shall they be attached to hoists except as specified in other subparts of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Employees work from a platform suspended from roof anchorages. What does Subpart M require of the anchorages their personal fall arrest equipment is attached to?

options.A: They must be independent of any anchorage being used to support or suspend platforms
options.B: They may be the same anchorages that suspend the platform
options.C: They may be any guardrail post on the roof
options.D: They must be attached to the platform's hoist

questions.explanation: Anchorages for personal fall arrest equipment "shall be independent of any anchorage being used to support or suspend platforms and capable of supporting at least 5,000 pounds (22.2 kN) per employee attached," or meet the qualified-person design option.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does Subpart M require the employer to provide for in the event of a fall by an employee using a personal fall arrest system?

options.A: Only a written incident report within 30 days
options.B: A call to OSHA before anyone touches the system
options.C: Prompt rescue of employees, or assurance that employees are able to rescue themselves
options.D: Rescue by the local fire department in every case

questions.explanation: "The employer shall provide for prompt rescue of employees in the event of a fall or shall assure that employees are able to rescue themselves."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What load must the anchorage for a positioning device be capable of supporting?

options.A: 1,800 pounds
options.B: At least twice the potential impact load of an employee's fall or 3,000 pounds, whichever is greater
options.C: The weight of the employee only
options.D: 500 pounds per employee attached

questions.explanation: "Positioning devices shall be secured to an anchorage capable of supporting at least twice the potential impact load of an employee's fall or 3,000 pounds (13.3 kN), whichever is greater."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A cover is placed over a hole in a site roadway that delivery trucks cross. What must the cover be able to support without failure?

options.A: The weight of one employee
options.B: 200 pounds applied at any point
options.C: The weight of the materials stored nearby
options.D: At least twice the maximum axle load of the largest vehicle expected to cross it

questions.explanation: "Covers located in roadways and vehicular aisles shall be capable of supporting, without failure, at least twice the maximum axle load of the largest vehicle expected to cross over the cover."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Warning lines and controlled access zones
questions.question: A roof uses a warning line system. Who may be in the area between the roof edge and the warning line?

options.A: Only employees performing roofing work in that area
options.B: Any employee who is carrying materials
options.C: Any employee, as long as a safety monitor is on the roof
options.D: Only supervisors and visitors

questions.explanation: "No employee shall be allowed in the area between a roof edge and a warning line unless the employee is performing roofing work in that area."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Warning lines and controlled access zones
questions.question: Where a controlled access zone is used for leading edge work, how must its control line run in relation to the unprotected or leading edge?

options.A: At a right angle to the edge
options.B: Along only the part of the edge nearest the work
options.C: Along the entire length of the edge, approximately parallel to it
options.D: In a loop around each employee at the edge

questions.explanation: "The control line shall extend along the entire length of the unprotected or leading edge and shall be approximately parallel to the unprotected or leading edge."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where must a safety monitor be in relation to the employee being monitored?

options.A: On the ground level below the work
options.B: On the same walking/working surface and within visual sighting distance
options.C: In a site office watching by video
options.D: On any level, as long as a radio is used

questions.explanation: "The safety monitor shall be on the same walking/working surface and within visual sighting distance of the employee being monitored," and close enough to communicate orally.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where must a copy of a fall protection plan, with all approved changes, be maintained?

options.A: At the employer's main office only
options.B: At the nearest OSHA area office
options.C: In each employee's personnel file
options.D: At the job site

questions.explanation: "A copy of the fall protection plan with all approved changes shall be maintained at the job site."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must the employer's written certification record of fall protection training contain?

options.A: The employee's name or other identity, the training date(s), and the signature of the trainer or the employer
options.B: Only the name of the training company
options.C: The employee's home address and phone number
options.D: A copy of the employee's test answers

questions.explanation: The record "shall contain the name or other identity of the employee trained, the date(s) of the training, and the signature of the person who conducted the training or the signature of the employer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.503, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)
